races.name: Shamrock Enterprises Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Captain Hanley
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two seconds and several top-six finishes at Good, the step up to 2m4f suits his staying profile and Phillip Enright is an excellent claiming partner; 26 days since last run is fine, and hood and tongue-tie combination suggests connections have him ready.|

runners_data.name: Chasing Blues
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Gavin Cromwell but worryingly absent for 418 days; the fade-in-finish flag combined with minimal recent track evidence makes him highly speculative, and the 418-day layoff is a serious concern for even the most patient investor of time here.|

runners_data.name: Colwyn Bay
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner for P J Rothwell, Dylan Robinson taking the ride; form reads poorly on paper with a fall and a distant 17th last time, but he is fit (19 days) and the pace dynamic revolves around his willingness to go forward — he sets up the race for others rather than winning it himself.|

runners_data.name: Ellis Brittle
runners_data.note: Completely lightly raced unknown quantity for J P Flavin with Jordan Canavan (7lb claimer) aboard; no meaningful form to assess, going and distance assessments unavailable — purely speculative, though the booking of an apprentice suggests connections are managing expectations.|

runners_data.name: Fou De Toi
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained with a solid placing record at Cheltenham and Leopardstown under Sean O'Keeffe; the 90-day absence is noted but this yard manages returns well, and the horse's class on Soft suggests he handles cut — the step to Good ground at Wexford needs proving but the ability base is unquestioned.|

runners_data.name: Great Entirely
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner, lightly tried at 0 wins from 3 on Good, but fit at 18 days; his tendency to pull and go forward combined with OR 92 means he is likely outclassed if the race develops into a proper contest, and his role is primarily as a pace-setter who shapes the race for more talented rivals.|

runners_data.name: Lastofthenatives
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with a point-to-point pull-up in the last run (75P) and form reading 55P — the pull-up is a genuine red flag over a stamina test of 2m4f on Good; W J Burke yard has no recent 14-day runners to calibrate confidence, and going/style assessments are unknown.|

runners_data.name: Majestic Horizon
runners_data.note: Unexposed five-year-old with two thirds on Good for P J Rothwell — the same yard as Colwyn Bay — with Tiernan Power Roche riding; two placed efforts at shorter trips suggest the step to 2m4f may be the key to unlocking improvement, and Good ground is clearly his surface.|

runners_data.name: Newbrook Diamond
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's prominent runner with a solid record of placing (two seconds, multiple thirds) across varying ground types; only one run on Good in the dataset but placed, and the 72-day break for a well-resourced yard is not alarming — he is a consistent hold-your-level horse who needs a contest to run into.|

runners_data.name: Seven Towers
runners_data.note: Cromwell's most reliable runner here with four places from five Good-ground starts and an excellent consistency record; Keith Donoghue rides and is well-suited to patient, prominent placing tactics — the lack of a win is the concern, but the race shape of a genuinely-run 2m4f is exactly what he needs.|

runners_data.name: Tomthescaffolder
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for De Bromhead with Darragh O'Keeffe, one of Ireland's strongest jockeys, in the saddle; form of 46-4 is modest but all three runs on Good ground show he handles the surface, and the 50-day break with this powerful yard is not concerning — the distance step from 2m to 2m4f is the key unknown.|

runners_data.name: Nile Star
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type with a fade-in-finish flag and three consecutive bottom-third finishes on Heavy; 139 days off and all form on Heavy/Soft makes the Good ground a genuine concern — Shane Markey is a 7lb claimer which does not help the profile.|

runners_data.name: Magical Sal
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for McBratney in fine recent form (7-5-3-6-5 in last five), fit at 19 days; four runs on Good showing consistent mid-pack form suggests no ground issues, but the form ceiling appears limited and the lack of any win is notable.|

runners_data.name: Midnight Musical
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse flagged as fading in the finish; form of 2000-5 with recent heavy defeats makes this hard to recommend — two Good-ground runs resulted in 5th and 2nd, showing the surface is fine, but the current form trajectory is downward.|

runners_data.name: Rosie Brown
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a fade flag, four Good-ground runs producing one third and three very poor efforts (22nd, 13th, 0); Josh Younge is a 7lb claimer with limited experience, and the combination of style, fade flag, and poor recent form makes her very hard to fancy.|

runners_data.name: Sea Feliz
runners_data.note: Mullins' complete unknown — no form, no jockey listed in the data, lightly raced and going/style unknown; the yard's strike rate and T14 of 4/30 means this horse cannot be dismissed on debut or early start, and unexposed Mullins runners in maiden hurdles consistently outperform market expectations.|

runners_data.name: Mind Eraser
runners_data.note: Another lightly raced unknown with a point-to-point pull-up (40P) in recent history and form reading 5-44; Mr S J Butler (7) is an amateur claimer, and the combination of limited form, amateur rider, and unknown style profile makes this one to observe rather than trust.|

races.paceDynamic: Colwyn Bay and Great Entirely are the two confirmed front-runners in a 17-runner maiden hurdle over 2m4f on Good ground at Wexford, and both are expected to press for the lead from the outset, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a solo procession. With Colwyn Bay showing a history of making the running and Great Entirely's profile equally aggressive, neither is likely to yield willingly, meaning the pace should be honest and sustained throughout the trip — a significant factor over this longer maiden distance. Captain Hanley and Newbrook Diamond sit prominently behind them, adding further pressure to the front group and ensuring there is no let-up for those anchored at the head of affairs. This race shape — a genuinely contested lead with a solid tempo — classically favours patient, well-settled mid-division or hold-up horses who can travel economically and produce a resolute late run, provided they have the class and stamina to close on a strong gallop over 2m4f.

watchPoints.text: Watch Great Entirely at the start — if he fails to stride on immediately and loses the lead to Colwyn Bay, the pace could drop sharply in the early stages, fundamentally changing the race shape from a contested gallop to a tactical crawl.

Colwyn Bay's form includes a recent fall (F) and a 17th-place finish — a jumping error or early exit would remove the primary pace-setter and hand Great Entirely a gift lead, altering the tempo dynamic entirely.

Mullins' Sea Feliz has no public form and no jockey listed — any significant market support in the ring pre-race should be treated as a significant intelligence signal, as this yard rarely runs unexposed maiden hurdlers without meaningful preparation.

Seven Towers has placed four times from five Good-ground starts without winning — watch whether Keith Donoghue attempts to be more positive from a prominent position rather than repeating the patient tactic that has produced four near-misses.

Fou De Toi returns after 90 days for Mullins — monitor paddock demeanour and market move; a horse of this class dropping into a Wexford maiden hurdle off a break is either cherry-picked for a quick win or still finding full form.|

races.name: Clearwater Construction Handicap Hurdle (0-100) (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Mount Ferns
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile for trainer E McNamara; 54 days off, has finished placed at this trip on good, but a field this big with only one genuine pace-setter makes a clean run from the rear very hard to guarantee.|

runners_data.name: Grey Gardens
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's five-year-old is the race's sole confirmed front-runner and can control the fractions under Sean O'Keeffe, though racing out of natural style means a solo lead role requires disciplined front-running rather than just lobbing up; 37 days since last run on similar ground.|

runners_data.name: Lakota Blue
runners_data.note: 354 days off the track is the dominant concern for Mr N McParlan's mount, yet the prominent racing style is naturally suited to tracking one lone pace-setter and the form over 20f on good suggests this trip could be on the short side; watch for rustiness early.|

runners_data.name: Oh So Charming
runners_data.note: Kevin Healy's claim helps the weight; the hold-up style has produced a win and multiple places from 15 runs on good-to-good ground, and 19-day turnaround with tongue-strap suggests trainer Queally has this horse ticking over nicely heading in.|

runners_data.name: You Done Well
runners_data.note: Wears tongue-strap and pads, Alan O'Sullivan (5) takes the ride; genuine hold-up performer whose best figures come when getting a strong pace to chase but has placed prominently too — 28 days ago produced a close fourth over a similar trip on good.|

runners_data.name: Kentucky Bluebird
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue in the saddle for Gavin Cromwell's yard; a true hold-up horse by nature, though with so many closers in this field it is unlikely to secure the deep-lying berth it needs, reducing the chance this style will be delivered as intended.|

runners_data.name: Tropical Twist
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner who fell and was pulled up on most recent starts; the hold-up profile on good ground showed promise at Leopardstown but fades flag is significant and 76 days off means fitness questions linger — needs a strong pace to aim at.|

runners_data.name: Glendine Billy
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes over for Anthony Mullins; an eight-year-old whose recent form shows repeated struggles with big fields, and while Slevin's experience is an asset, the horse's natural closer profile will be compromised by the volume of hold-up types crowding the back of this race.|

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: Liz Doyle's five-year-old carries the fades-in-finish flag and has finished in the 5-9 range consistently; Richard Deegan rides and the horse's hold-up tendencies will be squeezed into a midfield slot, which does not suit a finisher that already struggles to see races out.|

runners_data.name: Mr Macphisto
runners_data.note: Eoin Griffin sends out this eight-year-old who has not raced in 593 days — the longest absence in the field — yet his good-ground record over similar distances is genuinely strong (2W4P in 15 runs) and prominent style fits the pace shape; Ms N M Bradley (7) claims are a concern but the profile is right.|

runners_data.name: Dark Berkshire
runners_data.note: Carries the fades flag and was pulled up last time; P J Rothwell's six-year-old wears a hood and has run 19 days ago, yet the hold-up profile is being squeezed into a midfield slot it does not naturally want, and the combination of fading tendency plus loss of positional comfort is hard to overcome.|

runners_data.name: He Who Dares
runners_data.note: S Curling's five-year-old has not won in nine runs on good-or-equivalent ground, and the fades-in-finish tag alongside a 0-for-career record tells its own story; Phillip Enright takes the ride but the profile screams against a big-field, single-pace-setter scenario where you need to find room.|

runners_data.name: Mount Hotham
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's seven-year-old has finished 9th to 14th in every one of its last five runs, and the fades flag alongside four zeros in the form string makes it difficult to construct a scenario where this horse finishes in the first four; Paddy Hanlon (5) claims do not compensate for the form.|

runners_data.name: Esticky End
runners_data.note: Dylan Robinson rides for Tom McGuinness; an eight-year-old prominent type who has placed twice from 15 good-ground runs and is lightly weighted at OR 72 — if the race is run to suit those near the pace, Esticky End could outrun its odds without winning outright.|

runners_data.name: Syosset
runners_data.note: Alex Harvey's mount arrives from a long break (287 days, 119 firing days) with flat-track experience at Dundalk rather than jumps form; the hold-up profile being mapped to midfield adds another layer of uncertainty on top of a stamina and jumping question mark.|

runners_data.name: O'Grady Cracker
runners_data.note: No jockey listed yet is a concern; a four-year-old with a fades flag whose recent form figures read 9-8-0-0 — the hold-up profile in a race with one pace-setter and traffic throughout makes a good finish very hard to achieve, regardless of who rides.|

runners_data.name: Barrogstown Girl
runners_data.note: Jarlath Fahey's six-year-old brings a 2W5P record on similar ground and a prominent racing style that maps naturally onto this race shape; 51 days since last run (11 firing days) means fitness is expected, and the low OR of 88 with a clean jumping record makes her a legitimate contender in the lead-stalker bracket.|

races.paceDynamic: Grey Gardens is the one confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner field and, with no genuine rival to pressurise them, Sean O'Keeffe can control matters from the front at a sustainable gallop on good ground over 2m1½f at Wexford. The pace is unlikely to be scorching — this is a single pace-setter dictating rather than a contested lead — which creates a race where prominent-to-midfield horses travelling comfortably will have the clearest routes, while true hold-up horses forced to race in traffic will need everything to go right late. This field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically slot to the rear; Kentucky Bluebird, Glendine Billy, Syosset and others are genuine closers who are expected to race further forward than ideal, with Oh So Charming, You Done Well and Mount Ferns among those most likely to actually secure the positions closest to the pace. A controlled, single-pace-setter scenario at a fair but not brutal gallop most favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace — those who can track Grey Gardens and kick from the two-out flight without needing a sustained closing burst from the back of a big field.

Oh So Charming — Kevin Healy (7) is on a hold-up horse that needs a clean passage in a 17-runner field; if they are caught on the wide outside on the final turn, the seven-pound claim advantage will be wasted.|

Mr Macphisto — 593 days off the track is a significant fitness concern; even though the prominent style and good-ground profile fit perfectly, watch in the early stages whether the horse is travelling or laboured, as the long layoff could cost it at the business end.|

Lakota Blue — 354 days off and a step down from 20f trips; watch for any signs of rustiness in the parade ring or early in the race, as this could be a horse who needs the run but whose style fits the shape precisely if it arrives fit.|

races.name: Clearwater Construction Handicap Hurdle (0-100) (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Mountain Port
runners_data.note: Top-rated horse in the field at OR 100, but a full year since last run (365 days including a fall) and a confirmed hold-up style in a race with no strong pace to chase — 5yo for Kieran Purcell who has a cold recent strike rate, and the layoff combined with a genuinely crowded rear makes this a wait-and-see comeback.

runners_data.name: Kilt
runners_data.note: Won last time out 37 days ago over a similar trip on Good ground, Shane O'Callaghan claims 3lb, and Good going suits him (2W3P in similar conditions) — a natural hold-up type who finished well last time, he is one of the better credentialled runners here but will need a seam late given the congested rear.

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: Has a win over 2m1f on Good ground already on his card and J J Slevin is a major positive at this level — a hold-up operator by style, he last ran 28 days ago and goes well fresh-ish, but needs the pace to set up a run that may not materialise fully in this single-pace shape.

runners_data.name: Bossing It
runners_data.note: Placed at 2m1f on Good going last time for David O'Brien and is one of the yard's more active runners (T14: 1/5); hold-up style means he is vulnerable to a lack of pace, though his recent form figures show he can finish closer than his position suggests when things fall right.

runners_data.name: My Mate Tony
runners_data.note: Has a tendency to fade in the finish and carries headgear (t), which is a concern in a race where the pace may not be fast enough to suit his pattern — 37 days since last run, Peter Smithers claims 7lb, and the 0W0P Good-going record does little to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Hatfield Hammer
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, Paul Nolan has been in decent form (T14: 3/13), and he maps well on Good ground (14/15 sim-going runs) — the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) notes he is racing slightly out of role in this context, but as the sole pace-setter he controls his own destiny and that is a major asset here.

runners_data.name: Baby Fish
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's runner has the best trainer strike rate in the field by volume but a fade flag and poor Good-ground record (2/5 sim-going) blunt enthusiasm — an unknown-style type who last ran 56 days ago, the combination of going doubts and finishing tendency makes him hard to rely on.

runners_data.name: Hidalgo Des Mottes
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature whose nine-year-old profile says patient ride and late challenge, but the field is so hold-up heavy that he has been pushed into the midfield on the map — his best recent run was a 2nd on Good over 2m3f, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies because he almost certainly won't get the race run to suit him.

runners_data.name: Sneddy Eddie
runners_data.note: Form reads 000-0 and he fades in finishes — a true hold-up type by headgear and history who has been mapped to midfield through redistribution pressure rather than genuine tactical flexibility, trainer has a flat T14 record (0/3), and 60 days off adds further doubt.

runners_data.name: Bella Union
runners_data.note: Two wins in his last five including back-to-back victories at 2m1f-2m2f on Good, Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride for a McConnell yard with a solid base of runners — a natural prominent type who will travel just behind Hatfield Hammer and is ideally placed for the likely race shape; the age (10) is the only flag.

runners_data.name: Davitts Quay
runners_data.note: A 5yo with just three runs, form reading 070-, who carries a fade flag and has been pulled into the midfield by redistribution — his natural hold-up instincts mean he is unlikely to secure a forward berth, and with minimal form in the book Anthony Mullins will simply need him to learn on the job here.

runners_data.name: Brave Josee
runners_data.note: Best recent run was a 2nd on Good over 2m4f 24 days ago, which is a positive freshness angle for Kevin Healy (7) at a good weight (153lbs) — she is a genuine hold-up type by headgear and history who the map has nudged forward by necessity, and the fade flag is relevant in a race where the pace may cut up.

runners_data.name: Doyen Og
runners_data.note: Hasn't won in handicap hurdles and carries a fade flag alongside blinkers, 34 days since last run — the map shows him in midfield but he is a genuine hold-up type squeezed forward by the sheer weight of closers in this field, and the form figures (3490-P) do not inspire.

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Blinkers worn, 0W in 10 Good-ground runs, and form of /4P0-P — genuinely held up by nature but sits in the midfield cluster through redistribution, Denis Hogan has been busy (T14: 3/20) but this horse's record suggests he finds little when asked.

runners_data.name: Bob The Builder
runners_data.note: A 308-day layoff (47 days from a point run) and a hold-up style buried in a crowded rear by redistribution are the headline facts — finishing positions in the 5-9 range at various distances don't suggest a horse who fires off a long break, and the Sean Thomas Doyle yard is quiet (T14: 0/0).

runners_data.name: Notmiwadi
runners_data.note: No jockey declared which is an immediate flag, 277 days since last run, and form of /9778- tells a story of consistent mid-division finishes on Good ground — a hold-up type mapped to midfield by redistribution pressure who faces a big ask on comeback from a lengthy absence for John McConnell.

runners_data.name: Out Moll's Gap
runners_data.note: Form of 0/PP0- is as blunt as it gets, Phillip Enright rides, 78 days off, and she hasn't finished in the frame in any of her last five hurdle starts — naturally held up but redistributed to midfield, the Good-ground record (2/6) offers no encouragement for a turn around here.

races.paceDynamic: Hatfield Hammer is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-horse field and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival likely to push the early tempo — this means he can dictate a comfortable, sustainable gallop from the front without being pressured into burning excess fuel. Behind him, Bella Union is the only other legitimate prominent type who can realistically track him into the first bend, giving the race a controlled, single-pace complexion rather than a hot-speed scenario. The deep field is dominated by hold-up horses, but many of those — Hidalgo Des Mottes, Brave Josee, Sneddy Eddie, Doyen Og, Backinabit, Bob The Builder, and Davitts Quay — are true hold-up types compressed into the midfield on the map because there is simply no room for them all to settle at the rear; in reality they will be jostling for position throughout and their ability to execute their natural style will be compromised. This race shape — steady pace, lone leader, bunched midfield — clearly favours horses who can travel prominently or produce a smooth, well-timed forward move from the second half of the race, as the lack of strong pace makes it very difficult for genuine closers to find the momentum needed to mow down a fresh, uncontested leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hatfield Hammer Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hatfield Hammer is allowed to stride ahead unchallenged and Bella Union slots in behind without contest, the race is run at a controlled, honest pace that never truly tests the field until late.
scenarios.body: If Hatfield Hammer is allowed to stride ahead unchallenged and Bella Union slots in behind without contest, the race is run at a controlled, honest pace that never truly tests the field until late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Runs Them Down
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace set by Hatfield Hammer allows a prominent or just-off-the-pace mover to coast through the race and produce one fluent challenge from two out.
scenarios.body: If the steady pace set by Hatfield Hammer allows a prominent or just-off-the-pace mover to coast through the race and produce one fluent challenge from two out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled pace compresses the field enough that a well-positioned hold-up type finds a seam late and sustains a run from the home turn to the line.
scenarios.body: If the controlled pace compresses the field enough that a well-positioned hold-up type finds a seam late and sustains a run from the home turn to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Field Splits
scenarios.trigger: If a rival attempts to inject pace mid-race, disrupting Hatfield Hammer's rhythm and creating a genuine end-to-end test that brings stamina into play.
scenarios.body: If a rival attempts to inject pace mid-race, disrupting Hatfield Hammer's rhythm and creating a genuine end-to-end test that brings stamina into play.

watchPoints.text: Bella Union (Darragh O'Keeffe) is the key danger to watch — two recent wins at this exact trip on Good, prominent style suits the controlled pace perfectly, and if she tracks Hatfield Hammer smoothly from the front she could hit the line strongest of all.

Monitor how many of the redistributed hold-up horses — Hidalgo Des Mottes, Brave Josee, Sneddy Eddie — actually try to force a forward position early; if several of them do, a brief scramble for the prominent spots could briefly raise the tempo before settling, which would alter the shape.

Kilt's jockey Shane O'Callaghan (3lb claim) needs to position quickly from the draw — if he gets caught behind the midfield traffic jam created by eight-plus hold-up types competing for limited rear slots, the clean passage he needs late may simply not appear.

Hatfield Hammer's STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) is worth monitoring in-running — if he drifts back at any stage under Paul Nolan's instructions or finds himself hemmed in on the inside, the single-pace scenario dissolves entirely and the race becomes significantly more open.

Notmiwadi (no jockey declared, 277 days absent) and Bob The Builder (308-day layoff) are live non-runners or early withdrawals to check at the off — if either is scratched it reduces the rear-of-field congestion marginally but does not fundamentally alter the pace picture.

races.name: Curracloe Beach Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Benner Wenner
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old from Henry De Bromhead's stable with only one hurdles start on record — a below-par eighth on good — and a flagged tendency to fade late; style uncertain, making him a speculative runner at this trip.

runners_data.name: Doctor Elvis
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the mount on this Gordon Elliott-trained seven-year-old who ran second on good ground over 2m4f most recently — the strongest combination of jockey, trainer, and proven prominent style in the field; handles this going well and the step up to 3m½f looks within his compass.

runners_data.name: Glenary Prince
runners_data.note: Second De Bromhead runner ridden by Mike O'Connor, ran fourth over 2m4f on good last time — a clean prominent profile that suits the anticipated race shape, though two runs from a small yard leaves some form uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Lights
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for a small trainer (0/2 in 14 days) with a tongue strap fitted and only one hurdles run to assess; will need a strong pace and a clear run to show what he can do over this extended trip.

runners_data.name: Spill A Drop
runners_data.note: Unexposed six-year-old with a tongue-and-pad headgear flag and form reading F1-4P — the win is enticing but the pull-up and fall suggest fragility; style unclassified, so his tactical impact is genuinely unknown.

runners_data.name: The Boysofairhill
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, he will control the tempo from the front on his favoured good ground, but his form string (P1-580) and known fade make him vulnerable once challengers close; Shane Fitzgerald must judge the pace to give him any chance at 3m½f.

runners_data.name: Young Doran
runners_data.note: Promising five-year-old who finished second over 2m2f on good at his sole hurdles start — Tiernan Power Roche rides for P J Rothwell whose 14-day strike rate is modest but the horse's prominent style ideally suits the expected race shape here.

runners_data.name: Bridgie Browne
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-strap and carries the lightest weight at 151lbs; form of 8-0 over shorter trips is uninspiring, and while her instinct is to come from well off the pace, the congested hold-up group means she is mapped to midfield — an uncomfortable compromise that reduces her chance of landing a telling blow.

runners_data.name: Im A Dream Twister
runners_data.note: Amateur-ridden by Mr B T Stone (7lb claim) for a yard with no recent runners; two pointing pull-ups leave his hurdles ability entirely unknown, and the amateur booking at this level adds further uncertainty over 3m½f.

runners_data.name: Mambo Du Large
runners_data.note: Only four years old and raced yesterday — a significant freshness flag that must be noted; form of P70 with two runs on good is uninspiring, and from a hold-up position in the rear, the trip and quick reappearance make this very difficult to assess positively.

runners_data.name: Mayo Shirocco
runners_data.note: Long-absent hold-up type (445 days on the clock, last seen pulling up 229 days ago) from Colin Bowe's yard — has shown some ability over 2m4f on good in the past but the layoff and unknown current fitness make it hard to rely on him in a 14-runner maiden.

runners_data.name: Pacy Macie
runners_data.note: Amateur-ridden with a pull-up in the form and style unclassified — racing off 62 days since a pointing appearance and for a yard with no recent Flat/jump track record; carries too many unknowns to assess confidently in this shape.

runners_data.name: Talas Kera
runners_data.note: Carries a significant OR of 79 — well below the field — and is a true hold-up operator who has been pushed into a midfield mapping because the rear is over-subscribed; John G Carr's runner has shown minor placed form at shorter trips on good, but racing partly out of role at a ratings disadvantage makes this a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Vangaway
runners_data.note: Three consecutive finishes of 11th, 14th, and 11th on good ground paint a consistent picture of a horse who struggles to land a blow; from a hold-up position with a fade flag, this looks a difficult winning proposition in a competitive maiden at 3m½f.

races.paceDynamic: The Boysofairhill is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner maiden hurdle over 3m½f and is expected to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on good ground without any genuine pressure from a rival pace-setter. Behind him, prominent types Doctor Elvis, Glenary Prince, and Young Doran will look to track close to the action, while the field is heavy with hold-up horses — Bridgie Browne and Talas Kera are genuine hold-up operators who have been mapped to midfield simply because the rear is congested with Mambo Du Large, Mayo Shirocco, Vangaway, Phoenix Lights, and others. The Boysofairhill's known tendency to fade in the finish means the pace he sets will be honest enough to test the field over this trip, but without being truly punishing — a steady-to-moderate gallop that should compress the field heading into the straight. This shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader comfortably and pick up when it matters; closers will need traffic to clear and may not see daylight soon enough over this distance at this track. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the map can accommodate, and Bridgie Browne and Talas Kera are the most likely to be shuffled further forward than they would choose, compromising their natural finish.

scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If The Boysofairhill sets a sustainable gallop and a prominent tracker times their challenge to pick him off approaching the last.
scenarios.body: If The Boysofairhill sets a sustainable gallop and a prominent tracker times their challenge to pick him off approaching the last.

scenarios.trigger: If The Boysofairhill sets a genuinely modest pace and the prominent trackers fail to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: If The Boysofairhill sets a genuinely modest pace and the prominent trackers fail to close the gap in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Gets Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race, stringing the field out and opening a clear passage for a true hold-up type in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens mid-race, stringing the field out and opening a clear passage for a true hold-up type in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Midfield Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the field splits or bunches chaotically at pace, with the prominent horses getting caught in traffic and a midfield stalker arriving from an unexpected position.
scenarios.body: If the field splits or bunches chaotically at pace, with the prominent horses getting caught in traffic and a midfield stalker arriving from an unexpected position.

watchPoints.text: The Boysofairhill's fade tendency is the pivotal factor — watch whether Shane Fitzgerald allows him an uncontested lead at a true gallop or attempts to conserve him, as this decision will define whether prominent trackers can coast up to him or are made to work early.

With 14 runners over 3m½f, watch the first two furlongs for crowding and jostling among the prominent group — Doctor Elvis, Glenary Prince, and Young Doran will all want to track close to the leader, and any interference here could compromise the race for the strongest-fancied horses.

Mambo Du Large ran only yesterday and his presence in the field is a welfare-and-form watch — if he weakens quickly mid-race he could become an obstacle for hold-up horses making their run from the rear.

Bridgie Browne and Talas Kera are natural hold-up types mapped into midfield due to a crowded rear; watch whether they end up further forward than intended, which would effectively alter the race shape if they take a prominent position against their natural profile.

The amateur jockey bookings on Im A Dream Twister (Mr B T Stone, 7lb) and Pacy Macie (Mr B J Walsh, 7lb) are worth monitoring in running — in a 14-runner field at this trip, inexperienced riders can inadvertently dictate traffic patterns for the horses around them.

races.name: Slaney Valley Beginners Chase

runners_data.name: Cinammon Roll
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old showed two wins at around this trip on good ground (form 11 at the back of the string) but returns after 272 days off and, though a natural front-runner, is squeezed into a midfield slot here and must deliver on reappearance — fresh horses for Elliott can be ready but the lengthy absence is a notable query.

runners_data.name: Coyote Spirit
runners_data.note: Last ran just 18 days ago (6th on good) and carries Elliott's powerful yard backing, but this natural prominent racer finds the prominent berths over-subscribed and will need to produce a career-best jumping display from a constrained position — sim-going record of 5/12 with only one win on good limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Donnie Devito
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's six-year-old has posted five consecutive placed efforts at around this trip on good ground, showing relentless consistency, and though he typically wants to race close to the pace, the crowded prominent tier forces him further back than ideal — watch whether Danny Gilligan elects to push forward regardless.

runners_data.name: Duke Silver
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin's booking is a strong positive signal for Joseph O'Brien's runner, who won over 3m on good and was placed twice at 3m+ — the 64-day break appears acceptable for this yard, but being mapped away from his natural prominent berth in a busy field is a real tactical handicap at this trip.

runners_data.name: Eclipse Chaser
runners_data.note: Mullins' six-year-old is one of the few prominent horses who hasn't been redistributed, meaning Sean O'Keeffe can actually ride him to his strengths — a recent third (23f, good) and a solid sim-going record (6/9) suggest the conditions suit, and the trainer's T14 strike rate of 14/112 is bullish.

runners_data.name: Fillyoureye
runners_data.note: Mullins' second string here, but unseated and pulled up in two of the last four starts is a serious jumping reliability concern — a win over 23f on heavy is fine for the trip, but Brian Hayes faces a horse that has shown fragility at the fences and the good-ground record (3/9 sim) is modest.

runners_data.name: Jackson Lamb
runners_data.note: Won twice on good ground at around this trip (form 11) and hg:h suggests headgear works — Alex Harvey keeps it simple up close to the pace, which is exactly the right profile for this race shape, and a T14 of 0/11 for McConnell is the only slight reservation.

runners_data.name: Mickie Angel
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's eight-year-old has zero wins or places on good going from 13 attempts in similar conditions — that sim-going stat (0W0P, 2/13) is damning for the surface today, and being a natural front-runner pushed back into a midfield role with no going suitability makes this one very hard to recommend, despite Daniel King's effort.

runners_data.name: Pinot Gris
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner with hg:tp (tongue-tie and blinkers applied), De Bromhead/O'Keeffe combination, but recent form shows 15th, 12th, and 16th — all at shorter trips on softer ground — and today's step up to 2m3½f on good is a significant profile change that may or may not unlock a different horse.

runners_data.name: Silent Selector
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile with a fade warning; won over 2m on good (form 1) and placed twice in similar conditions, but the fade flag and a 54-day break suggest Philip Donovan will be waiting for a pace injection that Pinot Gris is unlikely to supply — O'Leary has only one runner in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Wing Back
runners_data.note: The youngest runner at four years old returning from 260 days off, with a win and a place in hold-up style but carrying another fade warning — a long break combined with a closing style in what shapes up as a steady-run beginners' chase makes Phillip Enright's task very difficult, and the 9th and 13th recent figures on good are not encouraging.

races.paceDynamic: Pinot Gris is the confirmed lone front-runner here, and with no genuine challenger for that role, Darragh O'Keeffe can dictate a measured, uncontested gallop over 2m3½f on good ground — a setup that historically rewards the leader at Wexford when the pace is controlled rather than pressured. Behind, Duke Silver, Donnie Devito, Coyote Spirit, and Mickie Angel are all natural prominent types who will be forced to race in a more restrained midfield position than they would prefer, creating a congested group tracking the pace but unable to express their true style. The hold-up horses Silent Selector and Wing Back sit deepest, but both carry fade warnings and will need a stronger gallop than Pinot Gris is likely to set to get competitive momentum into the finish. This field holds far more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — of those redistibuted, Eclipse Chaser and Jackson Lamb, already comfortably in their natural prominent slot, are best placed to get a ground-saving position, while Duke Silver (JJ Slevin) and Donnie Devito have the class to push through from a wider berth. The race shape strongly favours horses that can sit close to a steady pace and produce a clean jumping round — front-to-prominent profiles who are NOT racing out of role benefit most, as the hold-up brigade are unlikely to get the searching gallop they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pinot Gris Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Pinot Gris is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable clip and none of the prominent cluster applies sustained pressure before the home turn.
scenarios.body: If Pinot Gris is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable clip and none of the prominent cluster applies sustained pressure before the home turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Wears Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield pack — particularly Eclipse Chaser or Jackson Lamb — apply pressure from the third-last and force Pinot Gris to use energy earlier than planned.
scenarios.body: If the compressed midfield pack — particularly Eclipse Chaser or Jackson Lamb — apply pressure from the third-last and force Pinot Gris to use energy earlier than planned.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race — perhaps through a departure or a series of jumping errors — and the final circuit becomes genuinely attritional, producing a strong late run.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses mid-race — perhaps through a departure or a series of jumping errors — and the final circuit becomes genuinely attritional, producing a strong late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Jumping Errors
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or exits thin the field dramatically and the race becomes an error-strewn survival test over the final mile.
scenarios.body: If multiple fallers or exits thin the field dramatically and the race becomes an error-strewn survival test over the final mile.

watchPoints.text: Watch Pinot Gris's jumping closely — if De Bromhead's runner meets a fence wrong in the early stages and loses his lead, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the prominent pack behind will be fighting for a position nobody has been able to settle into.

Duke Silver (JJ Slevin) is a horse worth monitoring at the start: if Slevin elects to push forward aggressively to claim a prominent position rather than accept midfield, it immediately pressures Pinot Gris and transforms the race from a solo lead into a contested gallop.

Fillyoureye's jumping record — pulled up and unseated in two of four recent starts — makes her a real interference risk in a beginners' chase field; Brian Hayes will need to give her plenty of room, particularly at the downhill fences at Wexford.

Mickie Angel's complete absence of a placed run in 13 starts on good going is an unusually stark stats flag — backers should note this horse has consistently underperformed on this surface and the redistribution away from his natural prominent role compounds the concern.

The four-horse cluster of redistributed prominent types (Duke Silver, Donnie Devito, Coyote Spirit, Cinammon Roll) will all be jostling for the same ground in the first half-mile — watch for bumping and interference as riders attempt to establish early position, which could unsettle several horses simultaneously.

races.name: Molloy Metals Recycling Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Harry Des Ongrais
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from a lengthy 131-day absence, and the amateur claim of Miss S A Carter (7) brings significant added uncertainty; his form in similar going reads 4/15 with no wins or places, and 166lbs is a stern burden for a horse needing to find his feet from the rear.

runners_data.name: Nouvotic
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who set up today's dominant pace scenario; 8 runs on good ground with 4 wins and 5 places tells a clear story, though the STYLE_FIT tag (0.91) is a minor caveat if early traffic disrupts his rhythm — Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong positive here.

runners_data.name: Ma Jacks Hill
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy in the plate is an immediate upgrade for Gordon Elliott's six-year-old, who won last time out on good and shapes as the most dangerous genuine prominent type behind the leader; the tongue-strap is retained and 26 days' freshness suits.

runners_data.name: Watch The Weather
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent racer whose good-ground record reads 12/15 which is uninspiring in terms of raw wins, though two wins and four places show consistency; Danny Gilligan takes over and the trainer's modest 14-day strike rate of 1/4 is a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Antrim Coast
runners_data.note: Mike O'Connor rides a horse with a commendable four consecutive placed efforts on good ground, but 279 days off the track is a serious question over a 2m3½f chase; if fitness holds, the genuine prominence style and course-applicable form make this interesting if the race develops into a battle of wills up front.

runners_data.name: Itsalladream
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has recorded a consistent run of five-finishes on good ground, suggesting a pattern of finishing without threatening; Gavin Brouder's trainer has a 0/10 14-day record, and at 148lbs the burden does not help the cause of making up late ground.

runners_data.name: Bridie's Beau
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with tongue-strap and pads (tp), posting two pulled-up efforts in recent form; good-ground record of 6/15 with no wins or places on similar ground is a stark negative, and Conor Stone-Walsh faces a difficult task nursing this horse into contention.

runners_data.name: Rexem
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by nature but mapped at the back with two placed efforts on soft rather than good; Dylan Kidd (7) claims 7lbs which helps the weight but the trainer's 0/29 14-day record is deeply uninspiring, and the good ground here is slightly less familiar territory than his placed form suggests.

runners_data.name: Lisleigh Lad
runners_data.note: Alan O'Sullivan (5) claims for Ms Eleanor Broderick's yard which has no activity in the 14-day window (0/0); the horse has placed on good going at similar trips and sits on the cusp between prominent and midfield, giving him some tactical flexibility if the race fragments.

runners_data.name: Clonshire River
runners_data.note: Strong form on good going with 1 win and 7 places from 13 runs, and genuinely consistent at this level; the horse is a true hold-up type that the field's congestion has pushed into a midfield mapping — the 275-day absence is the standout concern, and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects the positional compromise he faces in this shape.

runners_data.name: Kings Jet
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose preferred berth is threatened by the volume of pace in this field; won over 23f on good at Gowran at OR 114 and the form is not without merit, but the redistribution to midfield (STYLE_FIT 0.90) means he needs a chaotic race to express himself, and 112 days off adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Vina Ardanza
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse reshuffled into midfield by the density of closers at the rear; the headgear-free profile and Josh Williamson (5) claim are modest positives, but the form string of 33P-4U and a 33-day return on good ground suggests inconsistency, and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects genuine positional difficulty in this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Nouvotic is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead expected to press hard, Henry De Bromhead's seven-year-old should control a measured, sustainable gallop throughout the 2m3½f trip on good ground at Wexford. Ma Jacks Hill, Watch The Weather, and Antrim Coast are all genuine prominent types who will want to race close to the pace, meaning the prominent berths behind Nouvotic will be fiercely contested from the off. The field carries more pace than the race shape can accommodate — Kings Jet is a natural prominent racer who is unlikely to secure that position given the competition for those early slots, while Clonshire River and Vina Ardanza are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield because the rear of the field is equally congested with like-minded types. A controlled, front-runner-led tempo on good ground over this trip at Wexford strongly favours horses that can race prominently and travel smoothly into the straight, rather than those forced to make up ground from behind or out of their natural position.

scenarios.title: Nouvotic Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Nouvotic dictates an uncontested, even gallop and prominent challengers pick up the tempo in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Nouvotic dictates an uncontested, even gallop and prominent challengers pick up the tempo in the straight.

scenarios.body: If Ma Jacks Hill, Watch The Weather, and Antrim Coast all contest the early prominent positions, creating enough pressure to undermine Nouvotic's controlled gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuinely hot enough to drain the leaders and a true hold-up horse finds the necessary clear run late.
scenarios.body: If the early pace proves genuinely hot enough to drain the leaders and a true hold-up horse finds the necessary clear run late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, a mid-race incident, or a horse running badly out of its redistributed position causes the race to fracture and opens a gap for a lower-rated runner.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors, a mid-race incident, or a horse running badly out of its redistributed position causes the race to fracture and opens a gap for a lower-rated runner.

watchPoints.text: Nouvotic's jumping fluency is critical — if Darragh O'Keeffe loses a clean rhythm at any point in the first circuit, the controlled gallop that underpins Scenario A collapses and the race opens up immediately.

The contest for prominent positions between Ma Jacks Hill, Watch The Weather, and Antrim Coast in the early stages could escalate quickly — any bumping, checking, or interference here will disadvantage multiple runners and could drastically alter the pace shape.

Antrim Coast returning from 279 days off is a significant fitness question; if Gavin Cromwell's horse weakens suddenly in the straight after sitting prominently, it creates traffic problems for horses travelling behind.

Kings Jet and Clonshire River are both racing out of their natural positions — watch whether either manages to secure a better-than-mapped position at the start, as it would materially alter the race shape away from the projected scenario.

Harry Des Ongrais is 131 days absent under an amateur rider at 166lbs — if he jumps poorly or loses his position early, he becomes an obstacle rather than a participant, and trailing horses in the hold-up group should be monitored for disruption.

races.name: Save The Date 7th August Ladies Day Handicap Chase (0-100)

runners_data.name: Tingarran Express
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with an excellent Good-ground record (12/15 starts, 2W7P) and proven form over 16-18f Good; Simon Torrens knows this horse well and the blinkers aid focus — the natural position just off Sampoet suits him perfectly.

runners_data.name: Ingenious Stroke
runners_data.note: Back after an extraordinary 1,386-day absence, but his form figures of 1-3-3-2 over fences on Good ground are strikingly relevant; Mr B T Stone takes the 7lb claim and the De Bromhead yard has been in form (5/40 over 14 days), making him a fascinating unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Temptationinmilan
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up type whose recent form (7-12-5-?-14) shows no wins or places on Good ground in 15 tries; Ms A T O'Reilly claims 7lb but the form profile makes it very hard to make a case over this trip.

runners_data.name: Giant Haystacks
runners_data.note: Prominent-travelling seven-year-old with tongue tie, who has placed on Good ground (3/22f, 4/20f); Ross O'Sullivan's yard has been active and Danny Gilligan's booking is positive — capable of sticking to prominent position under a confident ride.

runners_data.name: Le Malin
runners_data.note: Hold-up type off 554 days absent, but won over 2m4f Good on latest start and has placed on Good-ground chases multiple times; the long absence is a legitimate concern yet the form before the break was strong enough to keep him relevant.

runners_data.name: Sampoet
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who will lead throughout under Ben Harvey; carries the top weight (161lbs) and has run on Good ground in 11 of 12 starts, though his form figures (4-8-5-4-?) show he rarely wins from the front — his role is as the pace-maker who sets up the race for others.

runners_data.name: King's Son
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with two placed efforts at 2m on Good ground; J J Slevin is a high-quality booking for Seamus Neville but the horse has finished 15th and 16th on his last two wins attempts, suggesting the level of form needs to come right.

runners_data.name: Sledgehammer
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse by style — placed in midfield on the map because natural closers are in excess, meaning he is likely to race closer to the pace than ideal; his four recent runs on Good ground show consistent mid-pack finishes without threatening to win (0W0P).

runners_data.name: My Good Pal
runners_data.note: Prominent-tracking type with tongue-piece and a recent 2nd over 2m4f on Good ground; Gavin Cromwell's prolific yard (9/49 over 14 days) gives this horse a significant trainer angle, and the return to Good going after a heavy defeat last time looks well-timed.

runners_data.name: Ixigreczed
runners_data.note: A horse that has faded on the run-in in recent starts — a genuine finishing concern flagged — and one whose natural rear-of-field style places it in midfield here only because so many closers are competing for the same ground; the form figures (14-11-6-10-9) confirm a horse that struggles to land a blow.

runners_data.name: Hey Sir
runners_data.note: Uncertain style (marked U) with tongue tie, returning after 63 days (40 days since a point-to-point); three runs of which only one piece of Good-going form — Sean O'Keeffe's experience is an asset but the sparse recent data makes this hard to assess.

runners_data.name: Deadheat
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old natural hold-up type who has been pushed into midfield on the map due to overcrowding at the rear; off 347 days, much of his recent form is on Soft or Heavy ground, and his three Good-going runs show limited promise — freshness may help but the age and the ground shift are risks.

runners_data.name: Sunwalk
runners_data.note: Flags a tendency to fade in the closing stages — a serious concern in a 2m3½f handicap chase — and natural hold-up style places it further forward than it would ideally race; the form figures (9-?-2-11-?) include a Good-ground 2nd over 17f but the fading pattern is worrying.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old with tongue tie and blinkers, but the most credible of the redistributed hold-up horses — won over 2m4f Good 20 days ago and has placed 14/15 times on Good ground; Josh Williamson's 5lb claim helps offset the horse's need to race closer than ideal in this large field.

runners_data.name: Party Pack
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing tongue tie, whose form figures (7-8-5-?-7) show no meaningful placing on Good ground across 10 runs; J P Flavin's yard has had no winners from five runners over 14 days, and the redistribution into midfield compounds an already uninspiring profile.

runners_data.name: Luimneach
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with hood and tongue tie, returning from 33 days off; one placed effort from 15 Good-going starts and recent form of 5-?-2 includes a second on Soft, not Good — Charlie O'Dwyer's 3lb claim is a positive but the consistent Good-ground failure rate is a real concern.

runners_data.name: L'Amiral Fromentin
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type with a pacemaker hood, racing just three days after his last run — the turnaround is very sharp and worth monitoring on the morning for market confidence; three Good-ground placed efforts suggest ability if recovery is adequate.

runners_data.name: Driveonwill
runners_data.note: Prominent-going six-year-old with tongue tie, trained by Ross O'Sullivan (4/24 over 14 days); won over 2m on Good ground recently but two unseats in his last three runs raise jumping questions — if he travels and jumps cleanly from a prominent position he is a serious contender.

races.paceDynamic: Sampoet is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate from the off at what shapes up as a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 2m3½f on Good ground — no rival is likely to seriously challenge for the lead, meaning the pace will be honest but controlled rather than searching. Tingarran Express, Giant Haystacks, Ingenious Stroke, and Driveonwill will press forward in prominent positions just behind, creating a compact early group and ensuring the race is run at a genuine clip without becoming a sprint. The field is heavily skewed toward hold-up types — Sledgehammer, Ixigreczed, Deadheat, Sunwalk, Fr Gilligansvoyge, and Party Pack are all natural closers redistributed into midfield on the map because there is simply no room for every horse to settle at the back; in practice the rear of the field will be congested and those horses will race closer than ideal. This race shape — a steady single pace-setter, a prominent group pressing without real pressure, and a crowded midfield — strongly favours horses with tactical speed who can travel prominently or make a smooth move from mid-division, rather than pure hold-up types who need a true test to get a clear run at the field in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sampoet Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sampoet sets a comfortable tempo and the prominent trio of Tingarran Express, Giant Haystacks, and Driveonwill travel smoothly just off the pace.
scenarios.body: If Sampoet sets a comfortable tempo and the prominent trio of Tingarran Express, Giant Haystacks, and Driveonwill travel smoothly just off the pace.

scenarios.title: Pace Wobbles, Midfielders Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Sampoet's gallop is slower than expected and the race turns into a sprint from the home turn, allowing horses travelling mid-division to pick up ground.
scenarios.body: If Sampoet's gallop is slower than expected and the race turns into a sprint from the home turn, allowing horses travelling mid-division to pick up ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Sampoet sets a genuinely strong pace that stretches the field and the front-runners empty in the final half-mile, leaving a proper gap for closers.
scenarios.body: If Sampoet sets a genuinely strong pace that stretches the field and the front-runners empty in the final half-mile, leaving a proper gap for closers.

scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the large 19-runner field causes jumping errors or early trouble, thinning the field dramatically and leaving a survivor to benefit.
scenarios.body: If the large 19-runner field causes jumping errors or early trouble, thinning the field dramatically and leaving a survivor to benefit.

watchPoints.text: Driveonwill has unseated twice in his last three starts — watch his early jumping from a prominent position with 19 runners in the field; any mistake at an early fence could cause significant interference.

The 19-runner field creates severe congestion in the first-fence approach, particularly among the many redistributed hold-up types (Sledgehammer, Ixigreczed, Deadheat, Fr Gilligansvoyge, Party Pack) who will all be seeking ground early — watch for a pile-up scenario at the first.

L'Amiral Fromentin runs just three days after his last start — monitor the morning market and any scratchings; if connections are confident, the sharp turnaround could be a handler's angle in a race where freshness is rewarded.

Ingenious Stroke returns after 1,386 days off — his jumping may be rusty, particularly in a big field on Good ground, and a schooling mistake early would end any chance despite the strong historical form.

Sampoet has never won from the front (0W3P on Good, 0W overall in this form string) — if the pace collapses in the home straight rather than being sustained, watch how quickly the prominent group rounds him up and whether a horse like Tingarran Express or Giant Haystacks can kick clear before the closers arrive.
